speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
translation: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
line: Dwell on something and you get attached; attachment becomes wanting, and blocked wanting turns into anger.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
sanskrit: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
translation: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the ruin of understanding; and with understanding ruined, a person is lost.
line: Anger clouds judgement, clouded judgement loses memory, lost memory wrecks reason, and then you fall.
misuse: Not 'never feel anger'. It warns about anger that takes over judgement, not about naming wrongs.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
translation: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion; all-devouring and greatly harmful. Know this to be the enemy here.
line: It's desire, which turns into anger when blocked. Never satisfied, it is the real enemy here.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
sanskrit: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः । वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥
translation: One whose mind is not shaken by sorrow, who has no craving for pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.
line: Unshaken in sorrow, not craving in joy, free of clinging, fear and anger: that is a steady mind.
misuse: A steady mind still feels; it just isn't run by sorrow, fear or anger.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
sanskrit: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
translation: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
line: Whoever can ride out the surge of desire and anger, here and now, is steady and happy.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
translation: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.
prasang.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
sanskrit: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति ॥
translation: The person who gives up all desires and moves about free from longing, without the sense of 'mine' and without ego, attains peace.
line: Drop the cravings, the sense of 'mine' and the 'I' that keeps score. That's where peace is.
misuse: Dropping 'mine' is about possessiveness, not about loving your people less.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
sanskrit: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
translation: By worshipping, through his own work, Him from whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.
line: Doing your own work well can be your worship of the source of all life.
misuse: Work as worship doesn't mean overwork or tolerating exploitation.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

speaker: Arjuna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
translation: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
sanskrit: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
translation: Here, Arjuna, the resolute mind is one-pointed. But the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.
line: A decided mind is single and focused. An undecided mind splits into endless branches.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna reveals the ancient lineage of this teaching and why he comes into the world.
sanskrit: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः । अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥
translation: One must understand what action is, what wrong action is, and what inaction is; the way of action is deep.
line: What to do, what to avoid, when to hold back: the way of action is deep.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: The Lord's power and the yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna says he taught this yoga long ago, that he appears whenever goodness declines, and that he meets people on whatever path they come by. He calls the way of action deep.
prasang.lesson: Every path sincerely walked is met; goodness keeps finding a way back.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये । बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
translation: The understanding that knows action and withdrawal, what should and should not be done, what is to be feared and what not, bondage and freedom, that understanding is sattvic, Partha.
line: Clear judgement knows when to act and when to wait, what to fear, and what frees you.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
translation: Thus I have declared to you this knowledge, more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
line: I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
translation: Established in yoga, do your work, Dhananjaya, giving up attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
misuse: Even in success and failure doesn't mean indifferent to them; learn from both without being thrown.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

speaker: Arjuna
setting: Arjuna's doubts end; Sanjaya closes the dialogue.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचनष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत । स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥
translation: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed and I have regained my memory through your grace, Achyuta. I stand firm, my doubts gone. I will do as you say.
line: My confusion is gone, my clarity is back. I stand firm, free of doubt, and I'll act.
misuse: Not blind obedience: Krishna told him to reflect and choose (18.63), and Arjuna acts from his own clarity.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.
prasang.lesson: Clarity, once found, turns into action.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna on why people miss the divine and who turns to it.
sanskrit: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन । आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥
translation: Four kinds of good people worship me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise, best of the Bharatas.
line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Most are deluded by the play of qualities. Four kinds of good people turn to the divine: the distressed, the curious, those in need, and the wise.
prasang.lesson: Whatever brings you to the search, distress, curiosity or need, is welcome.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
sanskrit: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः । ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥
translation: I am the same to all beings; none is hateful to me and none dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.
line: I am the same towards all; no one is hated, no one favoured. Those who love me live in me.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Arjuna asks which way of devotion is best; Krishna promises what he does for those who turn to him.
sanskrit: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
translation: For those whose minds are absorbed in me, O Partha, I very soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and endless change.
line: Whoever rests their heart in me, I lift out of the drowning sea, and soon.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna on devotees who find joy together and the light he gives them.
sanskrit: तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः । नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥
translation: Out of compassion for them, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
line: Out of compassion, I live in their hearts and clear the darkness with the lamp of understanding.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: The yoga of devotion and its fruit
prasang.summary: Devotees talk of the divine with each other and find joy; out of compassion Krishna lights the lamp of knowledge in their hearts.
prasang.lesson: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, Kaunteya, do it as an offering to me.
line: Whatever you do, eat, give or endure, do it as an offering.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥
translation: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you truly, for you are dear to me.
line: Mind on me, heart devoted to me, you will come to me. I promise: you are dear to me.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna on the five causes behind every action.
sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
translation: The seat, the doer, the various instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fifth, providence: these are the five causes of every action.
line: Every result has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the efforts, and the unseen. You're one of them.
misuse: Not 'it wasn't my fault'. You own your part; you just aren't the only cause.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna reminds Arjuna of his duty as a warrior and what retreat would cost him.
sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
translation: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, then engage in the fight. Done this way, you will incur no wrong.
line: Hold pleasure and pain, gain and loss, win and defeat as equal. Then step in and act.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Why a warrior must fight: duty
prasang.summary: Krishna appeals to Arjuna's sense of duty and honour, then tells him to treat victory and defeat alike before he acts.
prasang.lesson: Decide from steadiness, not from fear of winning or losing.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
sanskrit: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
translation: One joined to this understanding casts off both good and bad results here. So devote yourself to yoga; yoga is skill in action.
line: Yoga is skill in action: doing the work well, without being bound by it.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
translation: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

speaker: Bhartrihari
setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Vairagya 51; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 3.82; Kosambi 1948 no. 308 (OCR match)

prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

speaker: Narrator
setting: Bhrigu's final discovery after four returns to his father.
sanskrit: आनन्दो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात्। आनन्दाध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । आनन्देन जातानि जीवन्ति । आनन्दं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । सैषा भार्गवी वारुणी विद्या । परमे व्योमन्प्रतिष्ठिता ।स य एवं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति ।
translation: He understood that joy is Brahman. From joy these beings are born, by joy they live once born, and into joy they enter at death. This is the wisdom of Bhrigu and Varuna, established in the highest space. Whoever knows this becomes established.
line: At last Bhrigu saw: from joy all beings are born, by joy they live, into joy they return.
verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Taitt. III.6

prasang.summary: Bhrigu asks his father Varuna to teach him what is ultimate. Varuna gives only a clue and tells him to reflect. Bhrigu comes back four times with answers (food, breath, mind, understanding) and each time is sent back to go deeper, until he discovers that everything is born from joy, lives by joy and returns to joy.
prasang.lesson: A wise parent lets a child discover the answer instead of handing it over.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna names the chief glories in which the divine shows itself.
sanskrit: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥
translation: Whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful, know that it springs from a spark of my splendour.
line: Whatever shines with excellence, beauty or power, see it as a spark of the divine.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna lists his manifestations: among lights the sun, among rivers the Ganga, and ends by saying any excellence is a spark of his splendour.
prasang.lesson: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

speaker: Yudhishthira
setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
sanskrit: धन्यानामुत्तमं किंस्विद्धनानां स्यात्किमुत्तमम् / लाभानामुत्तमं किंस्यात्सुखानां स्यात्किमुत्तमं धन्यानामुत्तमं दाक्ष्यंधनानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् / लाभानां श्रेय आरोग्यं सुखानां तुष्टिरुत्तमा
translation: Yaksha: 'What is the best of good fortunes? The best of riches? The best of gains? The best of joys?' Yudhishthira: 'Competence is the best fortune; learning is the best wealth; health is the best gain; contentment is the highest happiness.'
line: The best gain is health. The highest happiness is contentment.
verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section CCCXI (sacred-texts)

prasang.title_en: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

speaker: Bhishma
setting: Bhishma closes the story of Gautama, who killed the kind crane that had sheltered and enriched him.
sanskrit: कृतज्ञमनसा भाव्यं मित्रभावेन चानघ / मित्रात्प्रभवते सर्वं मित्रं धन्यतरं स्मृतम्
translation: Keep a grateful heart and a friendly spirit. Everything grows out of friendship; a friend is the greatest blessing.
line: Keep a grateful heart. Everything good grows out of friendship.
verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CLXXIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

prasang.summary: A destitute brahmin, Gautama, is fed and sheltered by a kind crane, Rajadharma, and made rich by the crane's friend. On the way home he kills his sleeping benefactor for food. Bhishma ends: there is atonement for many wrongs, none for ingratitude.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude is the root of every friendship. Betraying a benefactor poisons everything after.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
sanskrit: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे । देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
translation: A gift given because it is right to give, to one who does nothing in return, at the right place and time and to a worthy person, is called sattvic.
line: Give because giving is right, to someone who can't repay you, at the right time and place.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणोन हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
translation: It is never born and never dies; having been, it will not cease to be. Unborn, eternal, constant and ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain.
line: The self was never born and never dies. It is not killed when the body is.
misuse: Not a reason to skip mourning or to take loss lightly; it is comfort about what remains.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
sanskrit: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहायनवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि । तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
translation: Just as a person casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so the embodied self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.
line: As we drop worn-out clothes and put on new ones, the self leaves a worn body for a new one.
misuse: Not a way to brush off someone else's grief with 'they've just changed clothes'.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
translation: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes on to another body. The steady person is not bewildered by this.
line: Childhood, youth, old age: the body keeps changing. The wise aren't thrown by the next change.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
sanskrit: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः । न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
translation: Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, and wind does not dry it.
line: No weapon cuts it, no fire burns it, no water wets it, no wind dries it.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

speaker: Vasishtha
setting: Vasishtha on the fourth gatekeeper: good company (satsanga).
sanskrit: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥
translation: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph

prasang.title_en: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.
prasang.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
sanskrit: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
translation: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
line: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: whatever is offered with love, I accept.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

speaker: Arjuna
setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
translation: Arjuna said: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against his will, as if pushed by force?
line: Why do I do the wrong thing even when I don't want to, as if something forces me?
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
sanskrit: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
translation: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you will cross over all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.
line: Even if you were the worst wrongdoer of all, the raft of wisdom would carry you across.
misuse: Not 'understanding cancels the harm done to others'; it frees you to change and make amends.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
sanskrit: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन । ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥
translation: As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.
line: As a blazing fire turns wood to ash, real understanding burns away the hold of past actions.
misuse: Not a way to skip accountability; amends still matter.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
sanskrit: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् । साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥
translation: Even if one of very bad conduct worships me with undivided devotion, he should be regarded as good, for he has resolved rightly.
line: Even if you've done great wrong, the moment you turn wholeheartedly, count yourself among the good.
misuse: Not 'devotion erases harm done to others'; turning around still includes making amends.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on simple, wholehearted devotion.
sanskrit: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति । कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥
translation: He soon becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. Kaunteya, declare it boldly: my devotee never perishes.
line: Such a person soon turns good and finds lasting peace. Mark it: no one devoted to me is ever lost.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: A leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love is accepted. Offer everything you do; the divine hates no one, and even a wrongdoer who turns wholeheartedly is counted good.
prasang.lesson: Small offerings given with love matter; no one is beyond turning around.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज । अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
translation: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.
line: Lean on me alone. I will free you from every wrong. Don't worry.
misuse: This is not 'do nothing' or 'ignore your duties'. Krishna says it to a man about to act; it lifts fear, not responsibility.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
translation: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light is within, that yogi becomes one with Brahman and reaches the peace of Brahman.
line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
sanskrit: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
translation: The happiness that comes from contact of the senses with their objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is called rajasic.
line: Some pleasure tastes like nectar at first and poison in the end. Know which kind you're choosing.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
translation: One whose self is unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. Joined to Brahman by yoga, he enjoys undying happiness.
line: Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
sanskrit: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
translation: For the undisciplined there is no understanding and no steady contemplation. Without contemplation there is no peace, and for the one without peace, where is happiness?
line: Without inner discipline there's no clarity; without clarity, no peace; and without peace, where is happiness?
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः । लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
translation: One who acts offering all actions to the Supreme, giving up attachment, is not touched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is not wet by water.
line: Like a lotus leaf in water, do your work without letting the mess soak in.
misuse: Staying unstained isn't staying silent about wrongdoing at work; you can act and still keep your peace.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
sanskrit: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठंसमुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वेस शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
translation: As waters enter the ocean, which is ever being filled yet stays unmoved within its shores, so the one into whom all desires enter in the same way finds peace, not the one who craves desires.
line: Rivers pour into the ocean and it stays full and still. Let desires enter you the same way.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
sanskrit: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
translation: For one who is moderate in food and recreation, measured in effort at work, moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrow.
line: Moderate in food and rest, in work and play, in sleep and waking: that's how sorrow eases.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
sanskrit: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा । निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
translation: Surrendering all actions to me, with your mind on the inner self, free from hope and the sense of 'mine', fight with your fever gone.
line: Hand your work to something higher, drop the 'mine' and the hoping, and act with the fever gone.
misuse: Surrender here means letting go of anxious grasping, not handing over your judgement or responsibility.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
translation: Whatever a great person does, others do the same. Whatever standard that person sets, the world follows.
line: Whatever a respected person does, others copy. The standard you set is the one people follow.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna, listing the qualities that free us and those that bind.
sanskrit: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च । अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥
translation: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance belong to one born with the demonic nature, Partha.
line: Show-off, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance: the marks of a nature heading the wrong way.
misuse: A mirror for yourself, not a label to throw at others.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Divine and demonic qualities, and where they lead
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the divine qualities (fearlessness, truth, no anger, compassion, forgiveness, humility) and the demonic ones (hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, harshness), and reassures Arjuna he has the good ones.
prasang.lesson: Character is a list you can practise: courage, truth, kindness, no arrogance.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
sanskrit: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः । तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः ॥
translation: who is the same in pain and pleasure, at home in the self, to whom a clod, a stone and gold are alike, who is the same to the pleasant and the unpleasant, steady, the same in blame and praise,
line: Even in pain and pleasure, at ease in yourself; earth, stone and gold the same; praise and blame alike.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: One beyond the qualities does not hate moods when they come or long for them when they go, sits like a witness, and is the same in praise and blame, honour and insult.
prasang.lesson: Let moods come and go without fighting or chasing them.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the body as a field, and what true knowledge consists of.
sanskrit: अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् । आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः ॥
translation: Humility, freedom from pretence, non-violence, patience, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control,
line: No need for status, no pretence, no harm, patience, straightness, respect for teachers, purity, steadiness, self-control.
misuse: Patience and humility aren't silence in the face of mistreatment.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: The field and the knower of the field
prasang.summary: Krishna calls the body the field and the self its knower, then lists what real knowledge looks like: humility, no pretence, patience, honesty, clear sight of ageing and illness.
prasang.lesson: Real knowledge shows up as character: humility, patience, honesty.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
translation: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
sanskrit: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
translation: The wise see with an equal eye a learned and humble Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and one who eats dog-meat.
line: The wise see the same self in a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

speaker: Bali
setting: Bali, a king who has ruled for ages, sits by his window and wonders what it all adds up to.
sanskrit: पुनर्दिनं पुना रात्रिः पुनः कार्यपरम्पराः । पुनःपुनरहं मन्ये प्राज्ञस्येयं विडम्बना ॥
translation: Again day, again night, again the same chain of tasks. Again and again: to a thinking person, I feel, this is a mockery.
line: Day again, night again, the same tasks again, over and over. A thinking person feels mocked by it.
misuse: Bali's question starts his awakening. The answer he finds is not quitting but mastering the mind; pair with 6a.115.43.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph

prasang.title_en: Bali tires of endless days and asks his father's riddle
prasang.summary: The demon king Bali has ruled the three worlds for ages. One day at his window he realises he is doing the same things day after day, night after night, and asks what any of it adds up to. He remembers a riddle his father Virochana once told him: a vast realm ruled by a silent king and an all-powerful minister. The minister is the mind; win it over, by practice, and everything is won.
prasang.lesson: When life feels like a loop, the work is not more of it but mastering the mind that runs it.

ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 1, Karma-Yoga: Freedom, p. 101
speaker: Swami Vivekananda
setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, 1895–96, chapter 7: freedom.
translation: "Misery comes through attachment, not through work." As soon as we identify ourselves with the work we do, we feel miserable; but if we do not identify ourselves with it, we do not feel that misery.
line: "Misery comes through attachment, not through work."
verified_with: Verbatim match to Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda (Advaita Ashrama, Mayavati Memorial Edition) as published at https://www.ramakrishnavivekananda.info/vivekananda/volume_1/karma-yoga/freedom.htm; also matches en.wikisource.org (The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda) word for word

prasang.summary: Misery comes from attachment, not work. He attacks duty that has become a compulsion and asks for work done freely. The greatest people often die unknown, so seek no praise.
prasang.lesson: Be at rest, be free, and work.

speaker: Bhartrihari
setting: Opening verse of 'Advice to the Mind'.
sanskrit: परेषां चेतांसि प्रतिदिवसमाराध्य बहुधा प्रसादं किं नेतुं विशसि हृदय क्लेशकलितम् । प्रसन्ने त्वय्यन्तः स्वयमुदितचिन्तामणिगणो विविक्तः संकल्पः किमभिलषितं पुष्यति न ते ॥
translation: O heart, why do you enter into weariness, day after day trying to please the minds of others in so many ways, to win their favour? When you are at peace within, your own clear resolve rises by itself like a cluster of wish-granting gems: what wish of yours would it not fulfil?
line: Why exhaust yourself daily winning others' approval? Settle inside, and your own clarity grants every wish.
verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Vairagya 34; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 3.61

prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

speaker: Angiras
setting: Angiras on how the wise live.
sanskrit: प्रणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन् विद्वान् भवते नातिवादी । आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ॥
translation: This is the life that shines through all beings. Knowing it, the wise one does not talk over others. Delighting in the self, playing in the self, yet active, such a one is the best of the knowers of Brahman.
line: Knowing this, the wise stop arguing. Their joy is within, and they stay fully active.
verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Mundaka III.1.4

prasang.summary: Two birds sit on one tree: one eats the fruit and grieves, the other simply watches. When the anxious bird sees the calm one beside it, its sorrow falls away. The section goes on to praise truth, effort and freedom from craving.
prasang.lesson: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.

speaker: Seer
setting: Follows the call to enjoy by letting go: how to live and work.
sanskrit: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतꣳ समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥
translation: Doing your work here, you may wish to live a hundred years. For you there is no other way than this: done in this spirit, action does not cling to a person.
line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
verified_with: data tr.hi; data tr.en; cf. Müller SBE 1, Isa 2

prasang.title_en: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

speaker: Bhartrihari
setting: From 'On the Greatness of Time'.
sanskrit: रात्रिः सैव पुनः स एव दिवसो मत्वा मुधा जन्तवो धावन्त्युद्यमिनस्तथैव निभृतप्रारब्धतत्तत्क्रियाः । व्यापारैः पुनरुक्तभूत विषयैरित्थंविधेनामुना संसारेण कदर्थिता वयमहो मोहान्न लज्जामहे ॥
translation: Thinking 'it is the same night again, the same day', creatures run about in vain, busy as ever with the tasks they have set going; with work full of the same repeated things, tormented by this round of existence, alas, out of delusion we feel no shame.
line: Same night, same day, the same tasks on repeat. We run in circles and call it living.
verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Vairagya 78; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 3.44; Kosambi 1948 no. 316 (OCR match)

prasang.title_en: Vairagyashatakam: On the greatness of Time
prasang.summary: Time empties cities, houses and courts; the busy never notice it passing; parents and childhood friends become memories. The section ends with life as a play and death as the curtain.
prasang.lesson: Time is passing while you're busy; notice it before it's gone.

speaker: Bhasa
setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph

prasang.title_en: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

speaker: Arjuna
setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi); data tr.en compared

prasang.title_en: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasang.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.
prasang.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

speaker: Janaka
setting: Janaka, having chosen to keep ruling, talks gently to his own restless mind at night.
sanskrit: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
translation: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly (Nirnaya Sagar text, sa.wikisource); Vihari-Lala Mitra 1891 translation (Project Gutenberg) compared at the same chapter and paragraph

prasang.title_en: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

speaker: Sugriva
setting: Sugriva, who has lost his own wife and kingdom, steadies a grieving Ram.
sanskrit: व्यसने वार्थकृच्छ्रे वा भये वा जीवितान्तगे। विमृशंश्च स्वया बुद्ध्या धृतिमान् नावसीदति॥
translation: In disaster, in money trouble, in fear, even when life itself is at stake, the steady person who thinks things through with their own mind does not sink.
line: In loss, money trouble or fear, the steady person thinks it through and does not go under.
verified_with: data tr.en_src (19th-c. English, Dutt edition) checked against the Sanskrit

prasang.summary: Ram and Sugriva swear friendship before a fire. Sugriva shows Ram the jewels Sita dropped; Ram breaks down, and Sugriva comforts him: in trouble the steady person thinks it through, and a friend is the greatest refuge.
prasang.lesson: Two people in trouble can carry each other.

ref_label: Complete Works, Vol. 4, Writings: Poems: Hold on Yet a While, Brave Heart, pp. 389–390
speaker: Swami Vivekananda
setting: Poem 'Hold On Yet a While, Brave Heart', written to the Maharaja of Khetri.
translation: If the sun by the cloud is hidden a bit, If the welkin shows but gloom, Still hold on yet a while, brave heart, The victory is sure to come. … Not a work will be lost, no struggle vain, Though hopes be blighted, powers gone; … Then hold on yet a while, brave soul, No good is e'er undone.
line: Still hold on yet a while, brave heart, The victory is sure to come.
verified_with: Verbatim match to Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda (Advaita Ashrama, Mayavati Memorial Edition) as published at https://www.ramakrishnavivekananda.info/vivekananda/volume_4/writings_poems/hold_on_yet_a_while.htm

prasang.title_en: 'Hold on yet a while, brave heart' (poem to the Maharaja of Khetri)
prasang.summary: A short poem of encouragement to a friend. Clouds hide the sun for a while, summer always follows winter, and no honest struggle is wasted even when hopes fail.
prasang.lesson: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

speaker: Vidula
setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
sanskrit: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.
verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section CXXXVI (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

speaker: Vasishtha
setting: The sage Vasishtha to Bharat, shattered by his father's death and Ram's exile.
sanskrit: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
translation: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.
verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against Awadhi text

prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

speaker: The gods
setting: Frightened gods come to Vishnu and say plainly what they need.
sanskrit: वयं शरणमापन्नाः शरणागतवत्सल !। भयं नो मोहजं येन विनश्यति तथा कुरु ॥
translation: We have come to you for refuge, you who love those who come for shelter. Do what will make our fear, born of confusion, go away.
line: We have come to you for shelter. Please make this fear, born of confusion, go away.
verified_with: Sanskrit read directly; data tr.hi/tr.en

speaker: Bhartrihari
setting: From the section on the wicked: the impossible position of anyone who serves a master.
sanskrit: मौनान्मूकः प्रवचनपटुर्वातुलो जल्पको वा धृष्टः पार्श्वे वसति च सदा दूरतश्चाप्रगल्भः । क्षान्त्या भीरुर्यदि न सहते प्रायशो नाभिजातः सेवाधर्मः परमगहनो योगिनामप्यगम्यः ॥
translation: Keep quiet and you are dumb; speak well and you are a babbler or a windbag; stay close and you are pushy; keep away and you lack confidence; be patient and you are a coward; refuse to put up with things and you are ill-bred. The duty of serving another is deep indeed, beyond the reach even of yogis.
line: Quiet, you're dull; talkative, a show-off; patient, weak. Serving a boss is harder than yoga.
verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 58; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.58; Kosambi 1948 no. 35 (OCR match)

prasang.summary: A field guide to toxic people: the brilliant but cruel, the spiteful critic who turns every virtue into a fault, the boss nobody can please, and friendships that shrink like morning shade.
prasang.lesson: Recognise spite for what it is, keep your distance, and stop taking it personally.

speaker: Bhartrihari
setting: From the section on the wicked: how spite twists every virtue.
sanskrit: जाड्यं ह्रीमति गण्यते व्रतरुचौ दम्भः शुचौ कैतवं शूरे निर्घृणता मुनौ विमतिता दैन्यं प्रियालापिनि । तेजस्विन्यवलिप्तता मुखरता वक्तर्यशक्तिः स्थिरे तत्को नाम गुणो भवेत्स गुणिनां यो दुर्जनैर्नाङ्कितः ॥
translation: The modest are called dull; the devout, hypocrites; the pure, frauds; the brave, heartless; the thoughtful sage, a fool; the gentle speaker, servile; the spirited, arrogant; the eloquent, a chatterbox; the steady, weak. What virtue of the virtuous has the wicked not smeared?
line: To a spiteful critic, modesty is dullness and courage is cruelty. No virtue escapes them.
misuse: Not every criticism is spite; use it to stop taking malice personally, not to ignore fair feedback.
verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Niti 54; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 1.54

prasang.summary: A field guide to toxic people: the brilliant but cruel, the spiteful critic who turns every virtue into a fault, the boss nobody can please, and friendships that shrink like morning shade.
prasang.lesson: Recognise spite for what it is, keep your distance, and stop taking it personally.

speaker: Bhishma
setting: Bhishma on public slander, answering Yudhishthira's question about being insulted in an assembly.
sanskrit: परिवादं ब्रुवाणो हि दुरात्मा वै महाजने / प्रकाशयति दोषान्स्वान्सर्पः फणमिवोन्नतम्
translation: The person who speaks ill of others in front of a crowd only puts his own faults on display, the way a snake raises its hood.
line: Whoever runs others down in public only puts their own faults on display.
verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section CXIV (sacred-texts)

prasang.summary: Yudhishthira asks how to respond when a harsh fool abuses you in public. Bhishma: let it pass like a crow cawing; the slanderer only displays his own faults.
prasang.lesson: Careless critics show their own faults. Let their words pass like a crow's cawing.

speaker: Seer
setting: The creation story: last of all, dharma is made.
sanskrit: स नैव व्यभवत् तच्छ्रेयो रूपमत्यसृजत धर्मम् । तदेतत्क्षत्रस्य क्षत्रं यद्धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्मात् परं नास्त्यथो अबलीयान् बलीयाꣳसमाशꣳसते धर्मेण यथा राज्ञैवम् । यो वै स धर्मः सत्यं वै तत् तस्मात्सत्यं वदन्तमाहुर्धर्मं वदतीति धर्मं वा वदन्तꣳ सत्यं वदतीत्येतद्ध्येवैतदुभयं भवति ॥
translation: Still he did not flourish. So he created a higher form, dharma. Dharma is the power over power; nothing is higher than dharma. Through dharma even a weak man can stand up to a strong one, as with the help of a king. That dharma is truth. So people say of one who speaks truth, 'He speaks dharma,' and of one who speaks dharma, 'He speaks truth.' Both are the same.
line: Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.
verified_with: data tr.hi; cf. Müller SBE 15, Brih. I.4.14

prasang.title_en: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasang.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasang.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

speaker: Ram
setting: Ram sends young Angad as his envoy to Ravana's court.
sanskrit: बहुत बुझाइ तुम्हहि का कहऊँ। परम चतुर मैं जानत अहऊँ॥ काजु हमार तासु हित होई। रिपु सन करेहु बतकही सोई ॥
translation: Why explain much to you? I know you are very capable. Talk with the enemy in a way that gets our work done and is good for him too.
line: Speak with your opponent so the work gets done and it does them good too.
verified_with: Gita Press Hindi meaning in data (tr.hi), checked against the Awadhi text

prasang.summary: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no warrior can.
prasang.lesson: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.

ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
speaker: Prahlada (quoted by Draupadi)
setting: Draupadi quotes old Prahlada answering his grandson: is forgiveness better, or force?
sanskrit: न श्रेयः सततं तेजो न नित्यं श्रेयसी क्षमा / इति तात विजानीहि द्वयमेतदसंशयम्
translation: Force is not always best, and forgiveness is not always best. Know this for certain, my child: both have their place.
line: Force isn't always right, and forgiveness isn't always right. Wisdom is knowing which the moment needs.
misuse: Forgiveness never means accepting ongoing harm; this verse itself says it has limits.
verified_with: Ganguli, Vana Parva section XXVIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

prasang.title_en: Forgiveness or force: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
prasang.summary: In the forest, Draupadi asks why Yudhishthira does not answer injustice with anger, citing Prahlada's advice that neither force nor forgiveness is always right. Yudhishthira replies that anger destroys and forgiveness holds the world together.
prasang.lesson: Anger rarely heals anything; forgiveness has limits. Wisdom is knowing which a moment needs.

speaker: Vidura
setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
sanskrit: आर्जवेन नरं युक्तमार्जवात्सव्यपत्रपम् / अशक्तं मन्यमानास्तु धर्षयन्ति कुबुद्धयः
translation: A person who is straightforward, and modest because of it, is taken for weak by small-minded people, and they push him around.
line: Small minds mistake your honesty and modesty for weakness, and try to push you around.
misuse: Not a reason to stop being straightforward; a reason to hold firm boundaries.
verified_with: Ganguli, Udyoga Parva section XXXIX (sacred-texts)

prasang.title_en: Vidura Niti: timing, gain and loss
prasang.summary: Vidura teaches that good words land only at the right moment, that some gains are losses, that habits shape a person, and what people look for in a friend.
prasang.lesson: Speak at the right time, weigh gain against cost, and repeat what is good until it becomes you.

speaker: Bhartrihari
setting: From 'Censure of Craving': the poet to his own hope.
sanskrit: खलालापाः सोढाः कथमपि तदाराधनपरैः निगृह्यान्तर्बाष्पं हसितमपि शून्येन मनसा । कृतो वित्तस्तम्भप्रतिहतधियामञ्जलिरपि त्वमाशे मोघाशे किमपरमतो नर्तयसि माम् ॥
translation: I somehow put up with the taunts of the wicked while trying to please them; I held back my tears and laughed with an empty heart; I folded my hands even before people whose minds were numbed by money. Hope, futile hope, how much more will you make me dance?
line: I swallowed insults and forced laughter with an empty heart. Hope, how much longer will you make me dance?
verified_with: Wortham 1886 tr., Vairagya 6; GRETIL Chaukhamba text 3.4; Kosambi 1948 no. 150 (OCR match)

prasang.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
prasang.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)
setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
sanskrit: अरणीमग्निकामो वा मथ्नाति दहृयं मम / वाचा दुरुक्तं देवर्षे तन्मां दहति नित्यदा
translation: My heart is churned the way someone wanting fire churns a fire-stick. The harsh words my relatives say keep burning me, day after day.
line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
verified_with: Ganguli, Santi Parva section LXXXI (sacred-texts)

prasang.title_en: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron
prasang.summary: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
prasang.lesson: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

speaker: Ram
setting: Ram has lain on the shore for three days asking the ocean for a way across. No answer comes.
sanskrit: अवलेपः समुद्रस्य न दर्शयति यः स्वयम्। प्रशमश्च क्षमा चैव आर्जवं प्रियवादिता॥ असामर्थ्यफला ह्येते निर्गुणेषु सतां गुणाः।
translation: See the ocean's arrogance: he does not even show himself. Calm, forbearance, straightforwardness and gentle speech, these virtues of the good, are taken by the unworthy as signs of weakness.
line: Calm, patience, honesty and kind words: people who don't value them will read them as weakness.
misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.
verified_with: data tr.hi / tr.en_src

prasang.title_en: Ram at the ocean: humble first, firm after
prasang.summary: Ram lies on kusha grass by the shore for three days, asking the ocean for a way. Ignored, he tells Lakshman that patience is being taken for weakness and takes up his bow. The ocean rises, offers a way (Nala's bridge), and Ram releases the arrow elsewhere at its request.
prasang.lesson: Be humble first. When humility is taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop once you're heard.

speaker: Krishna
setting: Uttanka, furious that the war happened, threatens to curse Krishna for not stopping it.
sanskrit: कृतो यत्नो मया पूर्वं सौशाम्ये कौरवान्प्रति / नाशक्यन्त यदा साम्ये ते स्थापयितुमञ्जसा
translation: I made every effort earlier to bring the Kauravas to peace. But they could not be brought to agree, however I tried.
line: I tried hard to make peace. When people refuse to be reconciled, you can't force it.
verified_with: Ganguli, Asvamedha Parva section LIII (section number inferred from data offset; meaning read from the Sanskrit)

prasang.summary: Returning home after the war, Krishna meets the sage Uttanka, who is furious that Krishna let the cousins destroy each other and threatens to curse him. Krishna explains that he tried hard for peace and was refused, and calms him.
prasang.lesson: You can try your best for peace and still fail. Others' choices are not your guilt.

speaker: Kabandha
setting: Ram is lost and grieving; Kabandha tells him to seek Sugriva, who has also lost his wife and home.
